title: Choose Last Train's new visual world
question: Which world should define the complete iOS redesign?

options.label: Night Chronograph
options.lineage: precision night-running instruments and black ceramic chronographs
options.thesis: The departure becomes a deadline you can feel: one enormous time, one luminous progress arc, and everything else held below its signal.
options.viewport: A portrait iPhone surface with no dashboard chrome: 23:47 dominates the upper half, a precise arc shows the remaining window, and the departure stack rises directly beneath it.
options.risk: The precision-timer language could feel like a fitness app if station and route identity are allowed to recede.

raised.raise: A persistent edge index always names the current station, direction, and service-day scope.
The most important departure time owns the screen at genuinely monumental scale.
The same geometry folds coherently from full app to widget, Lock Screen, and Dynamic Island.

options.label: Signal Lens
options.lineage: modern railway signal optics and route-setting light paths
options.thesis: One live signal governs the night: light travels along a restrained route line until the chosen train becomes the only illuminated destination.
options.viewport: A vertical route beam connects station, direction, and four departures; the last train is the sole red optical event and a selected Fast Train pulses into the Island.
options.risk: This is the most naturally railway-specific direction, but signal imagery is also the most familiar and could become literal if overdrawn.

options.label: Luminous Timetable Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket timetables reconstructed as tinted glass slides
options.thesis: Each answer is a precisely raked glass strip on a lit golden bed, with state carried by reversal, weight, and fixed cells rather than card chrome.
options.viewport: A lateral rack of three departure slides crosses the portrait screen; one opaque reversed plate states the last train while the station scope is fixed above.
options.case: It identifies immediately with timetables and carries dense railway facts beautifully; Night Chronograph is clearer in one-handed, after-dark use.
options.risk: Its golden field and angled density can feel archival rather than genuinely current if the construction is timid.

options.label: Cathode Gauze
options.lineage: cathode numeral stacks behind fine bronze anode mesh
options.thesis: Every possible train remains as a dark ghost while the current answer strikes forward in a crisp, warm glow.
options.viewport: Oversized ghosted departure numerals fill the plane behind one sharply illuminated time, with selected and stale states expressed as glow and afterglow.
options.case: It matches the nocturnal urgency and makes state changes memorable; overlapping ghosts are less immediately readable than the assigned instrument.
options.risk: The orange phosphor can drift into retro-industrial spectacle and weaken scanning if too many ghosts remain visible.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder
options.lineage: nineteenth-century lexicon pages with guide words and shoulder indexes
options.thesis: The screen behaves like a precise reference page whose edge always states the range currently in view.
options.viewport: Departures become ranked entries beside a narrow station-and-direction shoulder index.
options.case: The reference hierarchy is excellent, but neither the audience nor the moment feels naturally bookish.
options.kept: A persistent edge index for station, direction, and service-day scope.
options.risk: It turns a glanceable night tool into something that asks to be read.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Fixed character cells update in a disciplined cascade while rows remain locked to time order.
options.viewport: A compact mechanical board fills the phone with four fixed departure rows.
options.case: It is instantly legible but is the literal railway treatment this redesign is meant to move beyond.
options.kept: Uncompromising fixed-column rhythm for every departure row.
options.risk: It reads as a polished replica instead of a new product identity.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: monumental typography behaving as weather and terrain
options.thesis: Departure numerals gather, disperse, and reform as time advances toward the train.
options.viewport: One enormous departure time breaks into a directional current above a quiet service list.
options.case: The scale is compelling, but continuous typographic weather conflicts with two-second trust and reduced-motion needs.
options.kept: The winning time deserves scale large enough to become the whole first impression.
options.risk: Motion can turn essential information into spectacle.

options.label: Miura Field
options.lineage: precision deployable sheets and linked aerospace folds
options.thesis: One compact answer unfolds into linked departure detail without losing the underlying geometry.
options.viewport: The last train sits as the compact packet and unfolds into the next services and route detail on demand.
options.case: Its responsive logic is strong, but the fold metaphor adds learning cost to an app designed for immediate answers.
options.kept: One geometry must survive every Apple surface without becoming a smaller unrelated design.
options.risk: Diagonal folds can compromise native scanning and touch predictability.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium dark-mode transit app with clean glass cards, SF Pro, blue accents, and familiar segmented controls.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional navigation title, station card, direction control, and stacked departure cards executed at high native polish.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately usable but visually interchangeable with many contemporary travel apps.
